title: The client lifecycle, the client record and your starting point

say: The client lifecycle, the client record, and your starting point.
This is the video for module 1 of Client Relationship Management.
Client relationship management, or CRM, is the set of habits and records you use to look after people who already buy from you, so they stay, buy again and recommend you.

panel.heading: CRM is habits first, software second
items: Look after clients who already buy from you
So they stay, buy again and recommend you
A good notebook and a routine is CRM

say: A tailor with a good notebook and a steady follow-up routine is doing CRM. A business with expensive software that nobody updates is not.
This module shows you the full cycle, what to record, and where you are starting from.

say: First, enquiry. She asks a question, sees your Status, or a friend refers her.

panel.heading: Five stages, round and round
items: Onboarding: agree item, price, deposit, date

say: Second, onboarding. You agree the item, the price, the deposit and the date. This is where expectations are set.

panel.heading: Five stages, round and round
items: Onboarding: agree item, price, deposit, date

say: Third, delivery. You do the work and record what was delivered.

panel.heading: Five stages, round and round
items: Onboarding: agree item, price, deposit, date

say: Fourth, after-care. A short check that she is happy, a care tip, a thank-you. Most small businesses skip this stage, and that is where they lose repeat clients.

panel.heading: Five stages, round and round
items: Onboarding: agree item, price, deposit, date

say: Fifth, repeat and referral. She orders again or sends a friend, and the cycle starts again with more trust.

say: Client lifetime value is how much one client is likely to spend with you over the whole time she stays.
The formula is average order, times orders per year, times the years she stays.

card.title: What one loyal client is worth

say: Bisi's average party order is about 25,000 naira.

card.title: What one loyal client is worth

say: Her regular clients order about 3 times a year. That is 75,000 naira a year.

card.title: What one loyal client is worth

say: They stay about 4 years. So one loyal client is worth about 300,000 naira.

card.title: What one loyal client is worth

say: A one-time client is worth 25,000. A loyal one is worth twelve times as much.
So Bisi decides a thank-you message and a reminder before the festive season is well worth a few minutes. Use your own real numbers, not a guess.

say: Once you have more than about ten clients, memory starts to fail. So give every client one record.
Write her name, phone and how she found you. Her order history with amounts. Her preferences, and the important dates she mentions.
Record every promise you made, like a free adjustment. And end with one next action and a date. A record without a next action is just history. With one, it becomes a plan.
Words like difficult are opinions. They do not tell your future self what to do, and they could offend a client who saw them.
A useful note is specific, factual, dated and short. It records what she said or did.
For example, Amaka, a tailor in Enugu, notes that Chioma was referred by Nkechi, dislikes sleeveless styles, and starts a new job on 1 July. Next action: fitting reminder on 20 June.
Update the record within 24 hours, while details are fresh.
First, take the ten-point self-audit in the lesson, and write your score down with the date.
Then choose a tool. A paper notebook works for a handful of clients.

panel.heading: Pick one home for client records

cards.d: Fine under about 15 clients, no data needed. Hard to search, and lost if the book is lost.
Free. Sort and filter in seconds, with backup to your Google account.
Tag chats like New order or Pending payment. Not a full record on their own.

say: Google Sheets is the best free step up. For example, Funmi sells liquid soap in Abeokuta to 46 clients. She scored 3 out of 10, so she chose Google Sheets.

say: Your client list is valuable and private. Set a screen lock on your phone.

panel.heading: Protect the phone that holds your clients
items: Set a screen lock: PIN, pattern or fingerprint
Record only what you need to serve her

say: Turn on two-step verification in WhatsApp, so no one can register your number on another phone.

panel.heading: Protect the phone that holds your clients

say: Use a strong password on your Google account and turn on 2-Step Verification.

panel.heading: Protect the phone that holds your clients

say: And do not record things unrelated to serving her, like gossip or health details she did not share for the order.

say: Never share a verification code, even with someone claiming to be from WhatsApp or your bank.

panel.rule: Never share a WhatsApp or SMS verification code with anyone.

say: To remember. CRM is habits first. Watch the after-care stage. Know what a loyal client is worth. Keep one factual record per client, ending in a next action and date. And secure your phone and accounts.

panel.heading: Remember
items: CRM is habits and records first
Five stages: most clients are lost at after-care
Lifetime value: order x orders a year x years
One record per client, ending in a next action
Secure your phone before storing client data

say: Now practise. Calculate your own client lifetime value and circle your weakest stage. Write full records for your three most recent clients. Then take the audit, choose your tool and turn on your security settings.
